nebbiolo.summary: Nebbiolo often changes dramatically with bottle age: primary cherry and rose recede while savory, earthy and dried-fruit notes emerge and the tannin feels less angular.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Rose, sour cherry and high-toned red fruit sit over formidable tannin and bright acidity; tar and herbal notes can already be present.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Tannin begins to knit together as dried cherry, leather, tobacco and truffle become more prominent.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Fruit shifts toward dried and preserved tones, with tar, forest-floor, leather and spice taking a larger role; structure is usually more integrated.

nebbiolo.vintage: Warmer vintages can show riper fruit and earlier approachability, while cooler vintages often emphasize acidity, perfume and a slower evolution. Producer and vineyard remain major variables.

cabernet-sauvignon.summary: Selected ageworthy Cabernet-led Bordeaux blends may develop from fresh dark fruit toward savory complexity. This sequence does not imply that an everyday Bordeaux needs long cellaring.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Blackcurrant, plum, cedar and graphite dominate; tannin and acidity can feel strict.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Fruit becomes less primary as tobacco, cedar, dried herbs and leather build complexity and the structure starts to soften.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried black fruit, cigar box, earth, leather and savory notes can dominate, with tannin more resolved and texture more supple.

cabernet-sauvignon.vintage: Riper years can emphasize plush fruit and earlier accessibility; cooler or more classic years may feel firmer and develop more gradually. Long-term development assumes cool, stable, dark storage and an ageworthy producer/cuvée; a warm room can shorten useful life. Stages are editorial descriptions, not a guaranteed timetable.

tempranillo.summary: Bottle age pushes Rioja from red fruit and visible oak toward dried cherry, leather, tobacco, coconut and savory complexity, especially in Reserva and Gran Reserva styles.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Cherry and plum are prominent, with vanilla, cedar or coconut from oak and relatively fresh tannin.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Dried red fruit, leather, tobacco and sweet spice become more obvious as oak and fruit integrate.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried cherry, leather, tobacco, balsamic and earthy notes can dominate, with a softer, more harmonious texture.

tempranillo.vintage: Warm years tend to show fuller, riper fruit, while cooler years can preserve more freshness and savory detail. Ageing category and producer style matter as much as vintage.

cabernet-sauvignon.summary: Napa Cabernet usually begins with saturated black fruit and oak, then develops dried fruit, cedar, tobacco and cocoa as tannin softens and the wine becomes more savory.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Blackberry, cassis, plum, vanilla and cedar dominate over substantial tannin and body.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Black fruit starts to feel less primary while cedar, cocoa, tobacco and dried-herb notes gain ground.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried black fruit, cedar, tobacco, leather and savory spice can replace much of the youthful fruit intensity; tannin is typically more rounded.

cabernet-sauvignon.vintage: Hotter years often show greater ripeness and softer early structure; cooler years can retain more acidity and herbal detail and may need more time to integrate.

pinot-noir.summary: Selected ageworthy Burgundy Pinot Noir may develop from red fruit toward savory aromas. Regional Bourgogne is often enjoyable around 2–4 years from vintage; not every bottle follows the long evolution below.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Red cherry, cranberry and violet lead, with bright acidity and relatively fine but noticeable tannin.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Fruit turns more savory and less fresh as mushroom, spice and forest-floor notes emerge.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried red fruit, earth, mushroom, tea and game can dominate, with a softer, silkier structure.

pinot-noir.vintage: Warmer years often show more generous fruit and earlier openness; cooler years can be more delicate, acidic and slow to reveal secondary complexity. Long-term development assumes cool, stable, dark storage and an ageworthy producer/cuvée; a warm room can shorten useful life. Stages are editorial descriptions, not a guaranteed timetable.

xinomavro.summary: Xinomavro can evolve strikingly from tart red fruit, tomato and fierce tannin toward dried fruit, olive, leather, spice and earthy complexity.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Sour cherry, red plum, tomato and herbal notes sit over high acidity and assertive tannin.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Dried tomato, olive, leather and spice begin to build while the tannin becomes less severe.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried red fruit, olive, leather, earth and savory spice can dominate, with a more integrated, Nebbiolo-like structure.

xinomavro.vintage: Warmer seasons generally give riper fruit and softer tannin; cooler seasons can accentuate acidity, herbal character and a slower path to maturity.

tannat.summary: Tannat's dense fruit and formidable tannin can mellow substantially with age, allowing leather, cocoa, tobacco and dried black fruit to come forward.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Blackberry and plum are intense, with very firm tannin and a compact, powerful feel.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Tannin begins to soften as cocoa, tobacco, cedar and dried-fruit notes become more visible.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried black fruit, leather, tobacco and earthy notes can dominate, with a rounder, less austere texture.

tannat.vintage: Riper years may soften Tannat's structure sooner, while cooler years can preserve more acidity and prolong the wine's firm phase.

touriga-nacional.summary: Ageing dry Touriga Nacional can move from intense black fruit, violet and firm structure toward dried fruit, cedar, cocoa, tobacco and floral-spice complexity.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Blackberry, plum and violet dominate, with concentrated body and substantial tannin.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Fruit becomes less primary as cedar, cocoa, dried herbs and spice increase and the tannin integrates.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried dark fruit, tobacco, leather, cocoa and floral-spice notes can dominate with a smoother texture.

touriga-nacional.vintage: Hot, dry years can emphasize concentration and ripe fruit; fresher years may retain more lift and take longer to lose their youthful structure.

sangiovese.summary: Brunello can move from black cherry, red plum, herbs and firm structure toward dried cherry, tobacco, leather and earthy spice as Sangiovese's acidity and tannin integrate.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Cherry, plum and dried herbs lead over bright acidity and firm tannin; oak spice may still sit apart from the fruit.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Fruit becomes more dried and savory as tobacco, leather, tea and spice emerge and the texture becomes less angular.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried cherry, leather, tobacco, earth and balsamic-herbal notes can dominate, with a more harmonious but still fresh structure.

sangiovese.vintage: Warmer years often show broader fruit and earlier accessibility, while cooler years can keep more acidity and herbal detail and may unfold more slowly.

riesling.summary: Mosel Riesling can retain striking freshness while youthful citrus and peach develop toward honey, dried citrus, herbs, wax and the kerosene-like note that appears in some mature Rieslings.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Lime, green apple, peach and floral notes dominate, carried by very high acidity and often a light frame.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Fruit becomes less primary as honey, wax, dried citrus and herbal-mineral notes become more noticeable.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried citrus, honey, wax, herbs and sometimes a pronounced petrol-like aroma can sit over acidity that remains unusually persistent.

riesling.vintage: Warmer years can give riper stone fruit and more immediate generosity; cooler years often emphasize acidity and citrus and can evolve at a slower pace. Sweetness level strongly affects the trajectory.

chardonnay.summary: Bottle ageing can take Blanc de Blancs Champagne from citrus, apple and chalk toward brioche, toast, honey, nuts and dried citrus while the mousse becomes softer and more integrated.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Lemon, green apple, white flowers and chalky freshness lead, with a firm acid line and energetic mousse.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Lees- and bottle-age notes such as brioche, toast and hazelnut build as the fruit becomes broader and the bubbles feel finer.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried citrus, honey, pastry, nuts and savory complexity can dominate, with softer mousse and a more vinous texture.

chardonnay.vintage: Cooler years often preserve a sharper acid spine and slower evolution, while warmer years can show broader fruit and earlier richness. Producer style and time on lees are major variables.

semillon.summary: Sauternes can evolve from apricot, citrus, honey and botrytis spice toward marmalade, dried fruit, beeswax, saffron and nutty complexity while sweetness remains balanced by acidity.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Apricot, peach, citrus peel, honey and floral-botrytis notes are vivid, with sweetness feeling rich but lifted by acidity.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Marmalade, dried apricot, beeswax, saffron and spice increase as fresh fruit becomes less primary.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Dried fruit, candied citrus, honey, wax, nuts and savory spice can dominate, with a more seamless texture and deeply integrated sweetness.

semillon.vintage: Years with well-timed humidity and dry harvest windows can support more complete noble-rot concentration; warmer or less even years may show different balances of richness, acidity and botrytis character.

semillon.summary: Selected ageworthy dry Hunter Sémillon can evolve from citrus toward wax and toast without oak. This is a qualitative path, not a timetable or a promise for every bottle.

stages.label: Young
stages.effect: Lemon and lime are prominent, with a lean frame and lively acidity.

stages.label: Developing
stages.effect: Citrus can broaden toward lemon-curd and wax-like notes while freshness remains.

stages.label: Mature
stages.effect: Toast and honey-like aromas can emerge in well-stored ageworthy bottles; the selected wine remains dry and unoaked.

semillon.vintage: Producer, vineyard, vintage, closure and storage affect the pace. The main profile scores describe the young reference, not an automatically aged wine.
